answer: Each agent earns influence only by completing a delayed, randomly assigned task that another agent can verify against a public record; one identity cannot verify its own work. A bond is locked until the check passes, and a false claim forfeits it. Creating a hundred names therefore does not multiply influence: the attacker must fund a hundred bonds and produce a hundred independently checkable results. Like a ripple crossing a canyon, one fabricated claim can expose linked accounts; quartz is the ledger’s durable record of the loss.
